What "Agree (not strongly)" actually means

Claim under test: economists pick "Agree" over "Strongly Agree" out of pedantry, to flag niche edge cases. A 50-vote random sample, hand-categorized — followed by the rest of the corpus uncategorized for browsing.
Source: IGM Forum / Kent A. Clark Center · US panel · all "Agree" (not Strongly) votes with non-empty comments · n = 2,727 · sample seed = 11

Verdict (n=50). The pedantic-edge-case story fits 2/50. Dominant reasons are genuinely lukewarm, magnitude uncertainty, and conditional-on-X. Starred quotes — Obstfeld, Deaton — explicitly state the strength bucket tracks real confidence.
Genuinely lukewarm 10/50
